title: Reconstructing fluid velocity fields from sparse sensors using a variational quantum algorithm
authors: Nhat-Quang Nguyen, Mohammad Mehedi Hasan Akash, Kourosh Shoele, Yanzhu Chen, Huixuan Wu
abstract: Reconstructing fields governed by nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) from sparse measurements is a challenging task because the governing equations are strongly nonlinear and observations are available at only a few locations. Fluid velocity fields are a representative case. In this paper, we propose a variational quantum algorithm that reconstructs the solution over the entire spacetime domain at once. Rather than marching in time, the method encodes the full discrete spacetime solution in a single variational quantum state, so that all time points are optimized jointly. The cost function combines a sparse-measurement mismatch term with a physics-informed PDE violation term, letting data and the governing equation constrain the solution simultaneously. We demonstrate the method on the one-dimensional Burgers and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equations using numerical simulations. The results suggest that variational quantum algorithms with a spacetime encoding scheme offer a compact framework for reconstructing nonlinear PDE dynamics.
summary: This paper proposes using a variational quantum algorithm to reconstruct entire spacetime fields governed by nonlinear PDEs from only sparse sensor measurements. By encoding the full solution into a single quantum state and minimizing a cost function that enforces both the physics and the data, the authors show a compact quantum framework for solving challenging inverse problems in fluid dynamics.
main_problem: Reconstructing complex, nonlinear physical fields, such as fluid velocity, from sparse, limited measurements.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that a variational quantum algorithm using a spacetime encoding scheme can reconstruct globally consistent solutions for nonlinear PDEs like Burgers and KS equations with low error.
method: They formulate the reconstruction as a constrained optimization problem solved by minimizing a cost function combining PDE violation and measurement mismatch, encoded into a parameterized quantum circuit.
model_or_system: The system involves fluid velocity fields governed by nonlinear PDEs (e.g., Burgers, KS equations) defined over a spacetime domain. The reconstruction is performed using quantum states to encode the full solution.
key_observables: Reconstructed velocity field $u(t, x)$; Root-Mean-Square (RMS) error.

main_assumptions: The solution admits a sparse representation in the accessible Hilbert space; the real-space approach uses finite-difference approximations, while the Galerkin approach assumes a sufficient basis (sine-only).
figures_summary: Figures show reconstructed velocity fields for the Burgers and KS equations at various resolutions, demonstrating the method's ability to recover the full field profile.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the challenge of sparse PDE reconstruction, details two VQA encoding methods (real-space and Galerkin-reduced-basis), formulates the combined cost function, and validates the approach using numerical simulations on Burgers and KS equations.
why_interesting: This work directly applies quantum algorithms to solve inverse problems in classical physics (PDEs), providing a template for using quantum computation to constrain and solve complex, high-dimensional physical dynamics.
